MCP authoring tools (document_editor_create/import/export). Create an empty document with one addressable paragraph; import markdown/HTML (text) or DOCX/ODT (base64) into a new document or as a content replacement of an existing one (optimistic concurrency); export to markdown/html text or docx/odt base64 packages — the agent's verification channel. Reuses DocumentMarkdownImporter/DocumentHtmlImporter/DocumentDocxImporter/DocumentOdtImporter and the matching exporters from Tempo.Blazor.DocumentFormats.

Semantic MCP block/table tools (document_editor_insert_block/delete_block/move_block/update_block/set_table_cell_text). Insert paragraph/heading/list/quote blocks into the body (order-value semantics) or table cells (index semantics), move/delete/replace blocks and set table-cell text; compile into canonical insertBlock/deleteBlock/moveBlock/updateBlock/setBlockAttribute operations applied through the same pipeline as document_editor_apply_operations. Operation patterns are pinned by the C#/JS convergence fixture.

MCP introspection tool (document_editor_describe_document) producing a structured, agent-friendly overview of a DocumentEditor document: blocks with stable semantic addresses (blockId, tableCellId, content-control path per docs/document-mcp-addressing.md), truncated plain text, tables with cell ids, tokens, content controls, headers/footers, plus concurrencyToken and contentDigest for optimistic concurrency.

MCP diff/redline tools: document_editor_diff_versions compares two saved versions (or a version vs. the current state) into a structured agent-friendly diff (summary counters, added/removed/changed blocks with word-level diff segments, redlineAvailable flag) via DocumentComparisonService; document_editor_export_redline exports the comparison as a DOCX with real w:ins/w:del tracked changes (DocumentRedlineDocxExporter) or a PDF rendered with review markup through the headless pipeline. Identical versions yield an empty diff and refuse redline export.
MCP tools for reading and saving document editor snapshots.
MCP write tools for applying DocumentEditor operation batches.

Visual-feedback MCP tools (document_render_preview / document_render_pdf): render a DocumentEditor document (by id or inline JSON) to per-page base64 PNG previews (pages selection, dpi, maxPages cap) or a WYSIWYG PDF (DocumentPdfExportOptions passthrough incl. page setup, review display mode and forensic watermark) via the headless pipeline (ITempoDocumentService). Fail-closed: font-catalog gaps produce an agent-friendly diagnostic instead of synthetic metrics.

Semantic MCP text/formatting tools (document_editor_insert_text/replace_text/delete_text/format_range/set_heading/set_paragraph_properties). Address blocks by blockId + optional tableCellId and text ranges as plain-text offset/length per docs/document-mcp-addressing.md; compile into canonical insertText/deleteText/addInlineMark/removeInlineMark/setBlockAttribute operations applied through DocumentOperationApplier + provider save — the same path as document_editor_apply_operations, preserving optimistic concurrency and collaboration convergence.

MCP template/assembly tools: document_editor_insert_token (TokenRun at a plain-text offset incl. computed expressions, optional key validation against IDocumentTokenValueProvider), document_editor_wrap_conditional (IF/ELSEIF/ELSE content-control chains via DocumentAssemblyMetadata + branch/expression updates), document_editor_insert_repeating_section (row template bound to a collection token), document_template_describe (tokens, conditional chains, repeating sections overview) and document_assemble_render (template + tokenValues → PNG/PDF via TempoDocumentService with IF/ELSE evaluation, repeat expansion and computed expressions). Authoring compiles into convergence-tested insertBlock/updateBlock/deleteBlock operations.

Publishes MCP-applied operation batches to the host collaboration stream so humans with the document open see agent edits live. Fail-open: publishing never throws — a broken backplane returns false and only logs.
Resolved font catalog for the document MCP render tools — the flat ReportPdfFontFace list (explicit faces + aliases + optional system fallback) the headless layout measures and embeds with.

DI registration for the opt-in MCP live co-editing bridge: AddTempoDocumentEditorMcpCollaboration registers TempoDocumentMcpCollaborationOptions and IDocumentEditorMcpCollaborationBridge (resolving the collaboration provider/backplane lazily). Publishing stays disabled until options.Enabled = true.

DI registration for the document MCP render tools: AddTempoDocumentEditorMcpRendering registers the headless document pipeline (AddTempoDocumentServices), the configured TempoDocumentMcpRenderOptions and the resolved ITempoDocumentMcpFontCatalog as idempotent singletons.

Default live co-editing bridge: joins IDocumentCollaborationProvider once per document as the named agent participant (cached session), broadcasts operation batches plus a presence cursor (agent name + color at the edited block) and publishes an envelope with SourceInstanceId to IDocumentCollaborationBackplane when registered. Fail-open with ILogger diagnostics.

Opt-in live co-editing configuration for the document MCP tools: Enabled (default false), agent identity (AgentId/AgentName/AgentColor shown in presence), SourceInstanceId stamped on backplane envelopes against echo, and host callbacks (OperationPublishedCallback/CursorPublishedCallback) e.g. for SignalR group pushes.

Default ITempoDocumentMcpFontCatalog: materializes TempoDocumentMcpRenderOptions into a flat font-face list once — explicit faces, alias duplicates, then well-known system faces (Windows Arial, Linux DejaVu Sans) registered under Arial plus the configured fallback aliases.

Render configuration for the document MCP tools: explicit ReportPdfFontFace list, font aliases (alias family mapped onto a source family's faces), optional system-font fallback (Windows Arial / Linux DejaVu registered as Arial + SystemFallbackAliases like Aptos), an ImageResolver seam for provider-backed assets and the MaxPreviewPages cap.
Shared JSON options for MCP tool input parsing and output formatting.

Builds the JSON envelope every wireframe MCP tool returns, so the LLM can reliably tell success from failure: { "success": true, ... } or { "success": false, "error": "...", "message": "...", "validationErrors": [...] }.

items.description: MCP tools for listing, reading and creating stored wireframe documents. Persistence (and therefore live-change notification) is delegated to the host-supplied providers.

Deterministically transforms a wireframe into an implementation-oriented brief: pages become sections, geometry becomes layout regions, connectors become navigation flows, and component usage is summarised — the artifact a plan/use-case consumes to build the real page.
One non-fatal lint finding about a wireframe element: which element it concerns, a stable machine-readable code, and a human-readable hint.

members.name: Code
members.description: Stable machine-readable warning code.

members.name: ElementId
members.description: Id of the element the warning concerns.

members.name: Hint

items.description: Applies a granular operation batch (add/update/remove elements, connectors and pages, set title and canvas size) to a wireframe document. Operations are applied in order; the first failure aborts the batch (callers apply to a copy and only persist on success).
Outcome of applying a granular operation batch to a wireframe document.

MCP write tools for building wireframes with granular operations, scaffold helpers, full-document authoring, and whole-document replacement. Writes validate before saving, support expectedModifiedAt optimistic concurrency tokens, return advisory warnings, and can use strict=true to reject prop and enum warnings.

members.name: wireframe_apply_operations
members.description: Applies an ordered operation batch. addElement and layout children can use either concrete type ids or role slugs; roles resolve through the active scope and target packs.

members.name: wireframe_scaffold
members.description: Creates a starter design for landing, list, detail, form, dashboard, or auth archetypes and validates before saving.

members.name: wireframe_author_document
members.description: Authors a complete wireframe document in one call: resolves element role values to concrete component types, normalizes enum casing, clamps off-canvas elements, validates, saves, and returns warnings.

members.name: wireframe_replace_document
members.description: Replaces the whole document with validated JSON, returns advisory warnings, and supports strict=true for prop/enum warning rejection.

items.description: Lints a single wireframe element's props against its component schema: unknown keys, wrong types, and invalid enum values. LintAndNormalize additionally rewrites enum values to their canonical casing, which lets an agent's near-miss input be accepted.

members.name: SuggestNearest
members.description: Suggests the closest known prop name for a misspelled key, or null when nothing is close enough.

members.name: Lint
members.type: static IReadOnlyList<WireframeLintWarning> Lint(WireframeElement el, WireframeComponentSchema schema)
members.description: Reports problems without changing the element.

members.name: LintAndNormalize
members.type: static IReadOnlyList<WireframeLintWarning> LintAndNormalize(WireframeElement el, WireframeComponentSchema schema)
members.description: Reports problems and normalises enum values on the element in place.
